data.completion_memo: W5 complete: tool.subagent delegation is a first-class approval-required built-in capability in the v1 tool matrix (12th tool in Settings BUILTIN_TOOL_IDS, contract {authorityMode:"run_subagent", requiresApproval:true, maximumTurns 1..=8 default 4}, CapabilityKind::Subagent with protocol mapping, side-effect class NonIdempotent, scope run.subagent). The call suspends the Run with the standard durable approval challenge; approve runs the child exactly once, reject returns a denied result. The child loop runs inside the subagent tool dispatch over the SAME frozen model gateway (Arc-gated into FrozenFileToolAuthorityContextV1) and the SAME durable broker: its tool calls settle through the normal broker flow, while its model turns are covered by the parent pass-level settlement, so a crash mid-child leaves the pass uncertain and automatic replay is forbidden. Isolation contract: fresh child conversation (task ≤16KiB + optional context ≤32KiB as one bounded user message), definitions restricted to read/search/list/grep/web_search/web_fetch/todo (SUBAGENT_CHILD_TOOL_IDS), no approval tools, turn budget default 4/max 8 with the agent-node convention that frozen values below the two-turn loop minimum execute with the minimum, 8 tool calls / 64K token caps, and depth capped at one because the subagent tool is excluded from child definitions AND a SubagentToolPortV1 guard rejects any non-allowed capability. Deadlines are enforced by a shared fail-closed predicate (subagent_deadline_expired) checked before the child starts and fenced on every child interaction against the frozen Run deadline. The child result returns {finalText, modelTurns, toolCalls, inputTokens, outputTokens} to the parent model loop; usage is recorded and attributed on the subagent evidence/card within the parent Run (deliberate v1 choice: pass-level aggregate usage totals count only direct parent model turns, while the child usage is durably visible per card). Service tool_activity_facts now emits the subagent.started plus subagent.completed/subagent.failed fact pair for the W7 collapsible timeline card. Critical broker fix discovered by the tests: nested child deliveries re-scanned the parent's in-flight subagent outbox and settled it as an abandoned uncertain dispatch; trusted-core gained deliver_pending_dispatch_for (shared deliver_outbox state machine) and the child port invokes invoke_v1_scoped so nested deliveries target exactly their own outbox while top-level deliveries keep the drain-all recovery semantics. Tests: pipeline integration for result return (approval suspend → approve → child read/search → finalText with usage accounting), depth/nesting denial with failure propagation into the parent loop (gateway definition rejection verified end to end), turn-budget exhaustion (never-finishing child script hits the model-turn-limit and surfaces an is_error result), deadline predicate unit test, and the exact freeze/approval contract test. Verification: desktop suite 150 lib tests + 2 integration tests green (exit 0); complete workspace cargo test green across every crate and target (bootstrap-helper 61, capability-host lib 9 + all milestones, local-store 74, portable-store 8, trusted-core lib 5 + milestone_04 13 + milestone_05 5 + milestone_10 43 + others, process 6 + 43, protocol 6 + 16) after also fixing two previously-unreached Windows test gaps (trusted-core project test thread-name path sanitization and the settings tool-count assertions updated to the 12-tool matrix). W5 does not ship the subagent timeline card UI itself — that is task 86 (W7) — but the committed event stream it consumes is complete.
data.description: Implement the tool.subagent delegation tool: the model delegates a bounded subtask to a fresh child agent run with an isolated context (task prompt plus a bounded relevant-context slice), a restricted read-only tool subset (read/search/list/grep/web_search/web_fetch/todo), a small turn budget (default 4, max 8), no approval tools, and its own usage accounting charged to the parent run. The child runs through the same frozen model gateway and durable broker; its activity commits as subagent.started/subagent.completed(subagent.failed) events and renders as a collapsible timeline card; the final text returns to the parent model loop as the tool result. Depth is capped (no nested subagents in v1), deadlines are enforced, and uncertain child outcomes are never silently retried. Output: working delegation with Rust integration tests (result return, budget exhaustion, deadline, denied tools, failure propagation).
